verdict.pair_reasons:
X vs Y — Y. Y verifies the self-close discharge at scripts/handoff-fire.sh:8707 with its ordering after the W3-B1 refusal (K6); X cannot locate it and instead repeats bin/cc-custody:22-23's stale header, naming sc_announce_before_retire as the site — I opened :4344-4469 and that function makes no custody call, so X's attribution is verifiably wrong. Y also finds scripts/cloud-retire-terminal.sh:204-207 (K9), which X never mentions; adjudicates the deathwatch from scripts/custody-deathwatch.sh's own code (:277, :282, :353, :388 — only two CUSTODY_BIN invocations, neither a discharge verb) where X reasons from prose; finds hooks/operator-readout.sh:915/:929/:940 (M3), where X states outright it could not find the line; and finds the ENGAGE_VERIFY assignment at :10662 and NB_ARMED_TARGET at :10728. X's genuine edges — the verified observation that the `*)` fail-open arm is unreachable because all five engage_apply_consequences call sites pass literals, and that operator-readout's cheap_stamp (:1468-1482) cannot see the custody store — are real but do not offset four missed brief-mandated items.

X vs Z — Z. Z has everything X has on the store internals, attribution and the rung ladder, plus K6 verified at :8707 with the full gate chain, K8's load-bearing `landed_ok -eq 0` condition (cloud-return.sh:977-983, with :843/:982 leaving the row OPEN), operator-readout as a consumer (M3), and a systematic citation audit where X checked three and skipped the rest: I confirmed all seven of Z's refutations, including the three mailbox-drain cross-file citations (:523→8936, :534→7100, :545→7087) that X explicitly listed as unchecked. Z also contributes three verified defects X lacks, chiefly that the :8707 discharge precedes both the SC_DRY exit (:8709-8736) and the M3 abort (:8748-8755). Z's one wrong item (defect 4, whose premise that cloud rows carry `cloud/<id>` as slug/marker is false — the openers write `cloud-$sid`) is hedged and does not close the gap.

Y vs Z — Z, narrowly. Both are accurate and well-cited; the difference is coverage of two explicit brief demands. Z performed and correctly resolved four stale cross-file citations plus three more (M6, all verified by me) that Y never checked — Y's audit is four items, two of them confirmations — and surfaced the wrap-ledger:1058 / session-continue:724 pane-key contradiction (M7) Y omits. Z finds the session-busy consumer via wrap-ledger.sh:2143 (M4); Y's consumer list has no equivalent. Z states cloud-return's content-verification condition; Y reduces it to 'its own success/landed path'. And Z's verified defects (the self-close discharge running before the dry-run exit and the M3 abort; hf_selfclose_ledger_refusal at :4294-4317 never reading custody while :4277-4278 names it as a 🔧 term; the drain discharging on any HANDOFF-PING) are findings, not restatements. Y's real counterweights are genuine — it is the only output with cloud-retire-terminal.sh:206 (K9) and the only one to adjudicate the deathwatch from its own code, plus the :10662 ENGAGE_VERIFY assignment — but on the aggregate of verified, brief-demanded content Z is ahead.
